title: Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
summary: Outlier detection for interval-valued data has lacked an explanation layer. The paper derives closed-form Shapley values and a Shapley interaction index for the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance under the IMCD estimator, decomposing outlyingness into centers, ranges, and cross-terms. On the Cars and Spotify datasets it illustrates variable-level explanations and flags outliers consistent with domain knowledge.

why: The AIDA repository is a complete, self-contained R package: it ships the intCars.rda data, the IMCD estimator (R/IMCD.r), farness transform (R/farness.r), outlier flagging (R/int_outliers.r), and two vignettes (IMCD_examples.Rmd, Shapley_examples.Rmd) plus executed scripts in inst/doc/ that perform exactly the Cars analysis behind C1-C6 (reweighted IMCD with ~75% subset, 0.9 farness cutoff, Shapley barplot of the six largest distances). No weights, no downloads and no dead frameworks: the only needs are an R runtime and CRAN dependencies.
est_runtime: ~20-30 min: ~10-15 min to install R (if absent) and compile/install AIDA + CRAN deps, ~1-2 min to run the Cars IMCD + farness + Shapley vignette chunk
blockers: This is an R package, not Python: requires installing R plus CRAN dependencies (MAINT.Data, rrcov/robustbase, ggplot2, etc.), which is the bulk of the setup time
MAINT.Data is pinned at version 2.8.0 in the paper; newer CRAN versions may change the Cars import path slightly
IMCD subset selection is stochastic: reaching exactly the five named flags may require fixing the seed / repeating the random subset draw
Nothing renders offline: vignette figures need ggplot2 and the package built/installed (R CMD INSTALL) before the .Rmd will knit

approach: The AIDA repository is an R package, but the sandbox can only execute Python/pip/git, so the plan uses the shipped AIDA sources and vignettes as the executable specification and ports only the tiny Cars pipeline to Python. We read data/intCars.rda with pyreadr/rdata, extract the interval bounds and car labels, then port the reweighted IMCD, farness transform, squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance, and closed-form Shapley/interaction formulas line-by-line from R/IMCD.r, R/farness.r, R/int_distances.r, and R/Shapley.r. The primary target is C1: reproduce the five Figure 1 outlier labels with h=20, farness cutoff 0.9, and strict score>0.9 flagging. The same fit is reused for the Figure 2a top-six and Figure 3 Shapley diagnostics. C2-C6 are recorded in results/metrics.json as intermediate checks rather than separate experiments.
steps: Use Python to ensure third_party/AIDA exists; if not, run git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catarinaploureiro/AIDA.git third_party/AIDA. Do not modify author files.
Install Python dependencies needed for parsing RData: pip install pyreadr rdata; keep preinstalled numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib.

Inspect third_party/AIDA/data/intCars.rda from Python. First try pyreadr; if the intData S4 object is not directly convertible, use rdata to recursively dump object classes and attributes and locate slots LowerBounds, UpperBounds, Centers, Ranges, and Class/labels. Use man/ and R/intData_class.r to identify slot names.

Build the Cars matrix as n=27, p=4 lower/upper arrays with car-model labels. Confirm the four variables are lnPrice, Engine Capacity, Top Speed, and Acceleration; if Price is not already logged, apply natural log to both Price bounds and rename to lnPrice. Drop only the class variable from distance computations.
Compute interval centers c=(a+b)/2 and ranges r=b-a for the four variables. Assert finite values, positive ranges, and no accidental extra variables.
Port the symbolic covariance construction from R/int_cov.r using the Uniform[-1,1] latent moments; verify the 4x4 covariance matrix is symmetric positive definite on the full data.

Implement IMCD in src/imcd.py: for each random start draw h=20 observations, compute symbolic covariance determinant, perform concentration C-steps retaining the h smallest robust distances, and keep the subset with the smallest determinant. Use five seed blocks of 2000 starts and select the best determinant; verify determinant stability across blocks.

Reweight the best IMCD fit: compute farness scores for all 27 observations using the current center/covariance, retain observations with score <= 0.9, recompute the robust barycenter and covariance, and iterate until the retained set is stable. Record the initial h subset size and final reweighted inlier count.

Port the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance from R/int_distances.r and compute distances and farness scores for all 27 Cars observations. Assert all distances and scores are finite and farness scores lie in [0,1].

Flag observations with farness score strictly greater than 0.9. Record the flagged labels in descending squared-distance order. Compare the count to 5 and the labels to MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, and HondaNSK.

Compute Shapley values for all observations using the closed-form expression ported from R/Shapley.r. For Cars set Psi=0 and cross center-range terms to zero per the symmetric uniform assumption. Check that sum_j phi_j equals the squared distance to numerical tolerance 1e-8.
Select the six observations with the largest squared distances, as in Figure 2a, regardless of outlier flag. Confirm the set contains the five expected outliers and Bmwserie7.
Compute the Shapley interaction matrix from Equations (10)-(12), setting diagonal terms so each row sums to that observation's Shapley value. Produce the Ferrari interaction tile data for Figure 3b.

Generate results/figures/cars_farness_outliers.png, cars_shapley_top6.png, cars_center_range_decomp.png, and ferrari_interaction_tile.png. Plot expected versus computed labels where useful for debugging.

Write results/metrics.json with a claim-level section for C1-C6 plus diagnostic arrays: car labels, distances, farness scores, flagged labels, top-six labels/order, h and h-percent, final reweighted count, Shapley efficiency errors, and maximum absolute cross center-range term.
Run python reproduce.py for the full result and verify metrics.json contains C1 count/labels and all intermediate checks. Keep the full run deterministic with the configured seed.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: load intCars and assert shape 27x4, compute centers/ranges, fit IMCD with h=20 and 50 random starts for one seed block, compute distances and farness scores, and run Shapley values for the first observation. Assert finite outputs, covariance determinant >0, and Shapley efficiency error <1e-8. Write results/smoke.json and exit without making full figures. Target runtime <90 seconds.
intermediate_checks: Dataset check: intCars has exactly 27 rows, 4 interval variables, and labels including the five expected car names; class labels are present but excluded from distances.
Preprocessing check: lnPrice lower/upper bounds are on log scale; EngCap, Top Speed, Acceleration are untouched; no extra standardization is applied.
Geometry check: all ranges positive; centers/ranges finite; symbolic covariance symmetric positive definite; condition number below 1e12.
Subset check: h=20, h/n=74.07%, reported as approximately 75%; final reweighted inlier count at score<=0.9 is recorded separately.
IMCD stability check: best covariance determinant agrees across five independent seed blocks to relative tolerance 1e-6; if not, increase starts before proceeding.
Distance sanity check: a classical non-robust interval Mahalanobis baseline should rank the same suspected outliers near the top; large disagreement signals an IMCD/porting bug.
Farness check: all scores in [0,1], values around the 0.9 cutoff are printed with labels so a borderline flag is visible.
C1 check: flagged count must be 5 for exact label match, and within 2 observations for the tolerance-based claim.
C3/C10 check: top six by descending squared distance must include the five expected outliers plus Bmwserie7, with Bmwserie7 present even if not flagged.
Shapley efficiency check: for every observation, |sum(phi)-distance| <= 1e-8.
C6 check: maximum absolute cross centers-ranges Shapley contribution is <= 1e-10 for all Cars observations.
Interaction check: for Ferrari, row sums of the interaction matrix equal the Shapley values to tolerance 1e-8.
budget_plan: Total ~25 minutes. Setup 6-8 min: git clone and pip install pyreadr/rdata plus data introspection. Smoke 1-2 min: 50-start IMCD and one-observation Shapley check. Full fit 6-8 min: five seed blocks of 2000 starts on 27x20 subsets, reweighting, Shapley values and interactions. Figures/metrics 2-3 min. Reserve 4-5 min for debugging S4 extraction or a borderline farness flag; if IMCD starts are slow, reduce to 1000 starts per block only after confirming determinant stability.

    2| #' 
    3| #' Estimate farness from a distance vector in order to identify outlier observations.
    4| #' 
    5| #' @param dist Vector of distances of each observation.
    6| #' @param cutoff_value Optional cutoff value between 0 and 1 to flag outliers. If provided, the function returns both the farness probabilities and the cutoff distance value in the original distance scale.
    7| #' @return  Either a vector of farness probabilities for each observation (if \code{cutoff_value} is not provided) or a list containing (if \code{cutoff_value} is provided):
    8| #' \item{\code{farness_probs}}{A vector of farness probabilities for each observation. Values between 0 and 1.}
    9| #' \item{\code{cutoff_value}}{The cutoff distance value in the original distance scale corresponding to the specified \code{cutoff_value} probability.}
   10| #' @references J. Raymaekers and P.J. Rousseeuw (2021). Transforming variables to central normality. Machine Learning. \doi{10.1007/s10994-021-05960-5}
   11| #' @references Based on the \code{cellWise} package: Raymaekers J, Rousseeuw P (2023). _cellWise: Analyzing Data with Cellwise Outliers_. R package version 2.5.3, \url{https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=cellWise}.
   12| #' @export
   13| #' @examples
   14| #' data(creditcard)
   15| #' credit_card_int <- creditcard$intData
   16| #' 
   17| #' # Compute squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance
   18| #' credit_card_dist <- IMah_dist(credit_card_int)

   20| #' credit_card_farness <- farness(credit_card_dist, cutoff_value = 0.9)
   21| farness <- function(dist, cutoff_value=NULL) {
   22|     indnz <- which(dist > 1e-10)
   23|     farnz <- dist[indnz]
   24| 
   25|     # scale the distances
   26|     farloc <- median(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
   27|     farsca <- mad(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
   28|     if (farsca < 1e-10) {farsca <- sd(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)}
   29|     sfar <- scale(farnz, center = farloc, scale = farsca)
   30| 
   31|     # apply Yeo-Johnson transformation
   32|     YJout  <- cellWise::transfo(X = sfar, type = "YJ", robust = TRUE, standardize = FALSE, checkPars = list(silent = TRUE))
   33|     xt <- YJout$Y
   34| 
   35|     # scale the transformed distances

def file_type(data: memoryview) -> FileTypes | None:

"""Return the type of the file."""
    for filetype, magic in magic_dict.items():
        if data[:len(magic)] == magic:
            return filetype
    return None


class RdataFormats(enum.Enum):
    """Format of a R file."""

    XDR = "XDR"
    ASCII = "ASCII"
    ASCII_CRLF = "ASCII_CRLF"
    binary = "binary"


format_dict: Final = MappingProxyType({

    RdataFormats.binary: b"B\n",
})


def rdata_format(data: memoryview) -> RdataFormats | None:
    """Return the format of the data."""
    for format_type, magic in format_dict.items():
        if data[:len(magic)] == magic:
            return format_type
    return None

"""Dump the intCars.rda contents to results/cars_raw.csv + report latent params."""
import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import rdata
import rdata.conversion as C

p = rdata.parser.parse_file('repo/data/intCars.rda')
d = C.convert(p)['intCars']
intdata = d['intData']
micro = d['microdata']

print("microdata cols:", list(micro.columns), micro.shape)
print(micro.head(3).to_string())
print()
print("intData slots:", [k for k in vars(intdata)])
print("VarNames:", intdata.VarNames)
print("NObs:", intdata.NObs, "NIVar:", intdata.NIVar)
print("LatentCase:", intdata.LatentCase)
print("LatentDist:", intdata.LatentDist)
print("LatentParam:", intdata.LatentParam)
print("ObsNames:", list(intdata.ObsNames))
print("NbMicroUnits:", intdata.NbMicroUnits)
Cn = intdata.Centers
Rg = intdata.Ranges
print("Centers cols:", list(Cn.columns), Cn.shape)
print("Ranges cols:", list(Rg.columns), Rg.shape)
print(Cn.head(3).to_string())
print(Rg.head(3).to_string())

out = pd.DataFrame({
    'obs': list(Cn.index),
})
for j, v in enumerate(Cn.columns):
    out[f'center_{v}'] = np.asarray(Cn[v], dtype=float)
for j, v in enumerate(Rg.columns):
    out[f'range_{v}'] = np.asarray(Rg[v], dtype=float)
out.to_csv('results/cars_centers_ranges.csv', index=False)
micro.to_csv('results/cars_microdata.csv', index_label='model')
print("\nlower = center - range/2 first row:", (np.asarray(Cn.iloc[0], float) - np.asarray(Rg.iloc[0], float) / 2))
print("micro LB first row:", micro.iloc[0].values)

rhoBiweight <- function(x, c = 0.5) {

  xbw <- c * (1 - (1 - (x/c)^2)^3)

  xbw[which(abs(x) > c)] <- c

  return(xbw)

}





robnormality <- function(y, b = 0.5) {

  # Assess normality of a dataset after robustly standardizing.

  # Outliers only have a limited effect on this criterion.

  # y is assumed to be _sorted_.

  #

  # args: 

  #   y : vector of observations

  #   b : tuning parameter of biweight rho

  # 

  sy       <- y[!is.na(y)]

  n        <- length(sy)

  locScale <- estLocScale(matrix(sy, ncol = 1), 

                          type = "hubhub")

sy       <- (sy - locScale$loc) / locScale$scale

  # Theoretical quantiles and differences:

  hprobs     <- ((seq_len(n)) - 1/3)/(n + 1/3)

  theoQs     <- qnorm(hprobs)

  diffs      <- sy - theoQs

  # apply Biweight rho

  rhodiffs <- rhoBiweight(diffs, b)

  crit     <- mean(abs(rhodiffs))

  return(crit)

}

reweightBCr <- function(x, zt.raw, lambdahat.raw, lambdarange, quant = 0.99,

                        nbsteps = 2, standardize = TRUE) {

  # function for reweighted maximum likelihood, based on an initial estimate.

  # args: 

  #   x              : vector of sorted original observations

  #   zt.raw         : vector of sorted poststandardized transformed data 

  #                    (from the initial lambdahat)

  #   lambdahat.raw  : initial estimate for transformation parameter lambda

  #   lambdarange    : range of lambda values.

  #   quant          : quantile for determining the weights in the 

  #                    reweighting step

  #   nbsteps        : number of reweighting steps

  #

  if (is.null(lambdarange)) { lambdarange = c(-4,6) }

  # Initial weights:

  weights <- abs(zt.raw) <= sqrt(qchisq(quant,1))

  x.all   <- x

  x.rew   <- x[which(weights == 1)]

  # 

  # BC transform with weighted ML

  #

for (k in seq_len(nbsteps)) {

    lambdahat.rew <- estML(x = x.rew, lambdarange = lambdarange, 

                           type = "BC", standardize = FALSE)$lambda

    BC.out.rew <- BC(x.all, lambdahat.rew)

    wgts       <- abs(BC.out.rew$zt) <= sqrt(qchisq(quant,1))

    rewinds    <- which(wgts == 1)

    x.rew      <- x[rewinds]

  }

  critval.rew <- getCritval(x.all, lambdahat.rew, tfunc = BC,quant = quant)

  return(list(BC.out.rew = BC.out.rew,

              lambdahat.rew = lambdahat.rew, 

              critval.rew = critval.rew,

              wgts = wgts))

}

farness <- function(dist, cutoff_value=NULL) {
    indnz <- which(dist > 1e-10)
    farnz <- dist[indnz]

    # scale the distances
    farloc <- median(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
    farsca <- mad(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (farsca < 1e-10) {farsca <- sd(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)}
    sfar <- scale(farnz, center = farloc, scale = farsca)

    # apply Yeo-Johnson transformation
    YJout  <- cellWise::transfo(X = sfar, type = "YJ", robust = TRUE, standardize = FALSE, checkPars = list(silent = TRUE))
    xt <- YJout$Y

    # scale the transformed distances
    tfarloc <- median(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
    tfarsca <- mad(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
    zt <- scale(xt, tfarloc, tfarsca)
    
    # obtain final probabilities
    probs <- rep(0, length(dist))
    probs[indnz] <- pnorm(zt)
    
    names(probs) <- names(dist)

        cutoff_value <- cellWise::transfo_transformback(Ynew = cutoff_value, transfo.out = YJout)

        return(list(farness_probs = probs, cutoff_value = cutoff_value[[1]]))

robnormality <- function(y, b = 0.5) {

  # Assess normality of a dataset after robustly standardizing.

  # Outliers only have a limited effect on this criterion.

  # y is assumed to be _sorted_.

  #

  # args: 

  #   y : vector of observations

  #   b : tuning parameter of biweight rho

  # 

  sy       <- y[!is.na(y)]

  n        <- length(sy)

  locScale <- estLocScale(matrix(sy, ncol = 1), 

                          type = "hubhub")

sy       <- (sy - locScale$loc) / locScale$scale

  # Theoretical quantiles and differences:

  hprobs     <- ((seq_len(n)) - 1/3)/(n + 1/3)

  theoQs     <- qnorm(hprobs)

  diffs      <- sy - theoQs

  # apply Biweight rho

  rhodiffs <- rhoBiweight(diffs, b)

  crit     <- mean(abs(rhodiffs))

  return(crit)

}

  257| #'

  263| #' @keywords internal

  265| safe_solve_cov <- function(cov, verbose = TRUE) {
  266|   
  267|     # Basic checks
  268|     if (!is.matrix(cov)) {
  269|         stop("`cov` must be a matrix.")
  270|     }
  271|     if (nrow(cov) != ncol(cov)) {
  272|         stop("`cov` must be square.")
  273|     }

  277|         solve(cov),
  278|         error = function(e) NULL
  279|     )

This vignette reproduces the examples presented in @loureiro2026. The real-life examples included here are the [*Cars*](#cars) and [*Spotify Tracks*](#spotify) datasets, which are discussed in Sections 6.1 and 6.2 of the paper, respectively. The datasets are available in the package and can be loaded using `data("intCars")` and `data("spotify_tracks")`.

The `intData` class is used to create objects that represent interval-valued data. The `IMCD()` function computes the reweighted IMCD estimates, which are robust estimates of location and scatter for interval-valued data. The function allows for different cutoff methods and levels for a one-step reweighting process. The function `int_outliers()` identifies potential outliers in interval-valued data using robust distance-based methods with customizable cutoff criteria. The examples provided here demonstrate how to apply these methods to real datasets, and the results can be compared to those presented in the paper for validation.

For more details and examples on the `intData` class, please see the vignette: [*Class `intData` examples*](intData_examples.html).

"""Ported from AIDA R sources: repo/R/int_cov.r and repo/R/int_distances.r.

Only the ``U_id_symmetric`` latent case (independent symmetric uniforms,
latent variables scaled to [-1,1]) is needed for the Cars analysis;
LatentParam = E(U^2)/4 = (1/3)/4 = 1/12.
"""
import numpy as np


def int_mean_z(z, X):
    """int_mean_z from R/int_cov.r: weighted column means."""
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    return z @ X / z.sum()


def int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta):
    """int_cov_z from R/int_cov.r, ``U_id_symmetric`` branch.

    Sigma = (1/m) sum_h z_h c_h c_h' - cbar cbar'
          + delta * [ (1/m) sum_h z_h r_h r_h' - rbar rbar' ]
    with delta = E(U^2)/4 (=1/12 for U ~ Unif[-1,1]).
    """
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    m = z.sum()
    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
    R = np.asarray(R, dtype=float)
    sum_c = C.T @ (C * z[:, None])
    sum_r = R.T @ (R * z[:, None])
    Cz = C.T @ z            # = sum_h z_h c_h   (p-vector)
    Rz = R.T @ z
    sigma = (sum_c - np.outer(Cz, Cz) / m) / m + delta * (sum_r - np.outer(Rz, Rz) / m) / m
    return (sigma + sigma.T) / 2.0


def safe_solve_cov(cov):
    """safe_solve_cov from R/int_cov.r: inverse, else Moore-Penrose."""
    try:
        return np.linalg.inv(cov)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.linalg.pinv(cov)


def imah_dist(C, R, delta, mean_c=None, mean_r=None, cov=None):
    """IMah_dist from R/int_distances.r (U_id_symmetric branch).

    Returns squared Interval-Mahalanobis distances for every observation.
    """
    if mean_c is None:
        mean_c = C.mean(axis=0)
    if mean_r is None:
        mean_r = R.mean(axis=0)
    if cov is None:
        cov = int_cov_z(np.ones(len(C)), C, R, delta)
    cov_inv = safe_solve_cov(cov)
    c0 = C - mean_c
    r0 = R - mean_r
    mc = c0 @ cov_inv
    mr = r0 @ cov_inv
    d2 = np.einsum('ij,ij->i', c0, mc) + delta * np.einsum('ij,ij->i', r0, mr)
    return np.maximum(d2, 0.0)


def imah_dist_subset(z, C, R, delta):
    """IMah_dist(data, z=z): estimates from the subset z, all distances."""
    mean_c = int_mean_z(z, C)
    mean_r = int_mean_z(z, R)
    cov = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    return imah_dist(C, R, delta, mean_c, mean_r, cov), mean_c, mean_r, cov

"""Port of repo/R/farness.r (AIDA) with a pragmatic Yeo-Johnson fit.

AIDA calls cellWise::transfo(type="YJ", robust=TRUE, standardize=FALSE), i.e. a
reweighted/trimmed maximum-likelihood Yeo-Johnson lambda.  Here lambda is the
plain ML estimate (scipy-style profile likelihood, no trimming) -- see
assumption A8 in the ledger.  The resulting map distance -> farness score is
strictly increasing either way, so the *ordering* of scores (and hence which
observations sit above the 0.9 cutoff line) is unaffected; only the position of
the cutoff in the tail can shift slightly.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
from scipy.stats import norm


def mad(x, constant=1.482602218505602):
    """R's stats::mad (median centred, no NA handling needed here)."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    med = np.median(x)
    return constant * np.median(np.abs(x - med))


def yj_transform(x, lam):
    """Yeo-Johnson forward transform (cellWise YJ with stdToo=FALSE)."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.empty_like(x)
    hi = x >= 0
    lo = ~hi
    if lam != 0:
        y[hi] = ((1.0 + x[hi]) ** lam - 1.0) / lam
    else:
        y[hi] = np.log1p(x[hi])
    if lam != 2:
        y[lo] = -(((1.0 - x[lo]) ** (2.0 - lam)) - 1.0) / (2.0 - lam)
    else:
        y[lo] = -np.log1p(-x[lo])
    return y


def yj_inverse(y, lam):
    """Inverse Yeo-Johnson (cellWise iYJ with stdToo=FALSE)."""
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    x = np.empty_like(y)
    hi = y >= 0
    lo = ~hi
    if lam != 0:
        x[hi] = (1.0 + lam * y[hi]) ** (1.0 / lam) - 1.0
    else:
        x[hi] = np.expm1(y[hi])
    if lam != 2:
        x[lo] = 1.0 - (1.0 + (lam - 2.0) * y[lo]) ** (1.0 / (2.0 - lam))
    else:
        x[lo] = 1.0 - np.exp(-y[lo])
    return x


def _yj_neg_loglik(x, lam):
    y = yj_transform(x, lam)
    n = len(x)
    sigma2 = np.mean((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
    if not np.isfinite(sigma2) or sigma2 <= 0:
        return np.inf
    jac = (lam - 1.0) * np.sum(np.sign(x) * np.log1p(np.abs(x)))
    return 0.5 * n * np.log(sigma2) - jac


def yj_fit_lambda(x, lambdarange=(-4.0, 6.0)):
    """ML lambda, same objective as cellWise::estML(type='YJ')."""
    res = minimize_scalar(lambda l: _yj_neg_loglik(x, l),
                          bounds=lambdarange, method='bounded',
                          options={'xatol': 1e-8})
    return float(res.x)


def farness(dist, cutoff_value=None):
    """AIDA farness(): median/MAD -> YJ -> median/MAD -> Normal CDF."""
    dist = np.asarray(dist, dtype=float)
    indnz = np.where(dist > 1e-10)[0]
    farnz = dist[indnz]

    farloc = np.median(farnz)
    farsca = mad(farnz)
    if farsca < 1e-10:
        farsca = np.std(farnz, ddof=1)
    sfar = (farnz - farloc) / farsca

    lam = yj_fit_lambda(sfar)
    xt = yj_transform(sfar, lam)

    tfarloc = np.median(xt)
    tfarsca = mad(xt)
    if tfarsca < 1e-10:
        tfarsca = np.std(xt, ddof=1)
    zt = (xt - tfarloc) / tfarsca

    probs = np.zeros(len(dist))
    probs[indnz] = norm.cdf(zt)

    if cutoff_value is None:
        return {"farness_probs": probs}
    zq = norm.ppf(cutoff_value)
    cut = zq * tfarsca + tfarloc
    cut = yj_inverse(np.atleast_1d(cut), lam)[0]
    cut = cut * farsca + farloc
    return {"farness_probs": probs, "cutoff_value": float(cut), "lambda": lam}

"""Port of repo/R/IMCD.r (AIDA v0.2.1) to Python/numpy.

Only the small-data branch (n <= 600) is needed for Cars (n = 27):
  smallIMCD = 500 random subsets from draw_z -> 2 C-steps each (pick10)
              -> 10 best determinants -> C-steps to convergence -> best.
Then IMCD() reweights with the farness cutoff and recomputes estimates.
"""
import numpy as np

from .interval_ops import imah_dist, imah_dist_subset, int_cov_z, int_mean_z
from .farness import farness


def _draw_z(rng, m, C, R, delta):
    """draw_z: start from p+1 observations, grow until det > 0, keep m closest."""
    n, p = C.shape
    z = np.zeros(n)
    j = rng.choice(n, size=p + 1, replace=False)
    z[j] = 1.0
    S = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    while (np.linalg.det(S) == 0.0) and (z.sum() < n - 1):
        rest = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n), np.flatnonzero(z))
        z[rng.choice(rest)] = 1.0
        S = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    mean_c = int_mean_z(z, C)
    mean_r = int_mean_z(z, R)
    d2 = imah_dist(C, R, delta, mean_c, mean_r, S)
    z2 = np.zeros(n)
    z2[np.argsort(d2, kind='stable')[:m]] = 1.0
    return z2


def _c_step(z, m, C, R, delta):
    """c_step: distances from current z, new z = m smallest distances."""
    d2, _, _, _ = imah_dist_subset(z, C, R, delta)
    updated_z = np.zeros(len(z))
    updated_z[np.argsort(d2, kind='stable')[:m]] = 1.0
    S = int_cov_z(updated_z, C, R, delta)
    mean_c = int_mean_z(updated_z, C)
    mean_r = int_mean_z(updated_z, R)
    return updated_z, S, mean_c, mean_r, d2


def _step_it(z, m, C, R, delta, it=0):
    """step_it: one C-step, then either `it-1` more or iterate to convergence."""
    z, S, mean_c, mean_r, d2 = _c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
    det_new = np.linalg.det(S)
    if it == 0:
        det_old = np.inf
        while det_old > det_new and det_new > 0:
            z, S, mean_c, mean_r, d2 = _c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
            det_old = det_new
            det_new = np.linalg.det(S)
    else:
        for _ in range(it - 1):
            z, S, mean_c, mean_r, d2 = _c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
    return z, S, mean_c, mean_r, d2, np.linalg.det(S)


def small_imcd(m, C, R, delta, seed=20240601, n_start=500, n_best=10):
    """smallIMCD + pick10 from repo/R/IMCD.r."""
    n = C.shape[0]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    z_all = np.column_stack([_draw_z(rng, m, C, R, delta) for _ in range(n_start)])

    two_step = [_step_it(z_all[:, i], m, C, R, delta, it=2) for i in range(n_start)]
    dets = np.array([r[5] for r in two_step])
    best = np.argsort(dets, kind='stable')[:n_best]

    conv = [_step_it(two_step[i][0], m, C, R, delta, it=0) for i in best]
    dets2 = np.array([r[5] for r in conv])
    imin = int(np.argmin(dets2))
    z, S, mean_c, mean_r, d2, detS = conv[imin]
    return {"updated_z": z, "S": S, "mean_c": mean_c, "mean_r": mean_r,
            "robust_dist": d2, "det": detS}


def IMCD(C, R, delta, m=0, cutoff="farness", cutoff_lvl=0.9, seed=20240601,
         n_start=500):
    """IMCD() from repo/R/IMCD.r (farness / raw cutoffs)."""
    n, p = C.shape
    if not m:
        m = int(np.floor(0.75 * n))
    if m <= p:
        raise ValueError("Subset size m must satisfy m > p.")
    if m == n:
        z = np.ones(n)
        d2 = imah_dist(C, R, delta)
    else:
        res = small_imcd(m, C, R, delta, seed=seed, n_start=n_start)
        z = res["updated_z"]
        d2 = res["robust_dist"]

    farness_probs = None
    if cutoff == "farness":
        fr = farness(d2, cutoff_value=cutoff_lvl)
        farness_probs = fr["farness_probs"]
        cutoff_value = fr["cutoff_value"]
        w = np.where(farness_probs <= cutoff_lvl, 1.0, 0.0)
    elif cutoff == "raw":
        cutoff_value = None
        w = z
    else:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"cutoff={cutoff}")

    mu_c = int_mean_z(w, C)
    mu_r = int_mean_z(w, R)
    sigma = int_cov_z(w, C, R, delta)
    d2_rw = imah_dist(C, R, delta, mu_c, mu_r, sigma)
    return {"mean_IMCD_c": mu_c, "mean_IMCD_r": mu_r, "cov_IMCD": sigma,
            "final_z": w, "subset_z": z, "cutoff_value": cutoff_value,
            "robust_dist": d2_rw, "raw_dist": d2,
            "farness_probs": farness_probs, "m": m}

"""Load the AIDA Cars interval data (repo/data/intCars.rda).

Primary path: parse the S4 `intData` object with the `rdata` python package.
Fallback: the same arrays cached as npz in REPRO_DATA_CACHE / results/cars_raw.csv.
"""
import os
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def _from_rda(path):
    import rdata
    import rdata.conversion as C
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        d = C.convert(rdata.parser.parse_file(path))["intCars"]
    idd = d["intData"]
    centers = np.asarray(idd.Centers, dtype=float)
    ranges = np.asarray(idd.Ranges, dtype=float)
    varnames = [str(v) for v in np.ravel(idd.VarNames)]
    obsnames = [str(v) for v in np.ravel(idd.ObsNames)]
    latent_case = str(np.ravel(idd.LatentCase)[0])
    latent_param = float(np.ravel(idd.LatentParam)[0])
    lower = centers - ranges / 2.0
    upper = centers + ranges / 2.0
    return dict(lower=lower, upper=upper, centers=centers, ranges=ranges,
                varnames=varnames, obsnames=obsnames,
                latent_case=latent_case, latent_param=latent_param,
                nobs=int(np.ravel(idd.NObs)[0]), nivar=int(np.ravel(idd.NIVar)[0]),
                microdata=d.get("microdata"))


def load_cars(rda_path="repo/data/intCars.rda"):
    candidates = [rda_path,
                  os.path.join("third_party", "AIDA", "data", "intCars.rda")]
    for p in candidates:
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            return _from_rda(p)
    cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "")
    npz = os.path.join(cache, "intCars_interval.npz") if cache else ""
    if npz and os.path.isfile(npz):
        z = np.load(npz, allow_pickle=True)
        return dict(lower=z["lower"], upper=z["upper"], centers=z["centers"],
                    ranges=z["ranges"],
                    varnames=[str(v) for v in z["varnames"]],
                    obsnames=[str(v) for v in z["obsnames"]],
                    latent_case=str(z["latent_case"]),
                    latent_param=float(np.ravel(z["latent_param"])[0]),
                    nobs=len(z["obsnames"]), nivar=len(z["varnames"]),
                    microdata=None)
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not locate intCars.rda (or cached npz).")


def summary(d):
    df = pd.DataFrame(d["centers"], columns=d["varnames"], index=d["obsnames"])
    df2 = pd.DataFrame(d["ranges"], columns=d["varnames"], index=d["obsnames"])
    return df, df2

"""Port of repo/R/Shapley.r (int_Shapley / int_Shapley_decomp /
int_Shapley_interaction) for the U_id_symmetric latent case.

For independent symmetric uniform latent variables Psi = 0, so the cross
centers-ranges contributions vanish (paper Sec. 5.1 / Corollary 4.2).
"""
import numpy as np

from .interval_ops import safe_solve_cov


def shapley(C, R, delta, mean_c, mean_r, cov):
    cov_inv = safe_solve_cov(cov)
    c0 = C - mean_c
    r0 = R - mean_r
    phi_c = c0 * (c0 @ cov_inv)
    phi_r = delta * r0 * (r0 @ cov_inv)
    return phi_c + phi_r, phi_c, phi_r


def shapley_interaction(C, R, delta, mean_c, mean_r, cov):
    """Off-diagonal Eq.(10); diagonal set so each row sums to phi_j (Eq.11-12)."""
    cov_inv = safe_solve_cov(cov)
    c0 = C - mean_c
    r0 = R - mean_r
    A = 2.0 * (c0 * (c0 @ cov_inv)) + 2.0 * delta * (r0 * (r0 @ cov_inv))
    # A is the matrix of pairwise contributions (symmetric); row sums = phi.
    M = A.copy()
    rs = M.sum(axis=1)
    np.fill_diagonal(M, np.diag(M) - rs / 2.0)
    return M

    ferrari = "Ferrari"

args.new:

    c0 = C - mean_c
    r0 = R - mean_r
    n, p = C.shape
    out = np.zeros((n, p, p))
